root_causes.root_cause: LLM audit judge applies image-enrichment-completeness criterion to hierarchical (non-flat) documents, but classify_verdict at helpers.py:1244 only tracks image_enrichment_ratio for flat docs (content_class flat_prose/flat_mixed via the image_enrichment_promoted gate at line 1274). For hierarchical docs (content_class='' or 'unknown'), classify_verdict is called at client.py:1518 with image_enrichment_ratio=None and content_class='', so unenriched <!-- image --> markers in tree node text are invisible to the code-level gate. The stored verdict correctly returns PASS (502 nodes, depth 4, good max_leaf_ratio), but the LLM audit judge sees 12 unenriched image markers and downgrades to MARGINAL. This is a gate-vs-judge alignment gap, not a code bug in classify_verdict itself.
root_causes.code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/helpers.py::classify_verdict -> src/pageindex_mcp/client.py line 1518 (hierarchical doc verdict call)
root_causes.suggested_fix: Either (a) extend classify_verdict to accept an image_marker_count / unenriched_marker_count for hierarchical docs and apply a soft penalty (e.g., downgrade to MARGINAL if unenriched_ratio > threshold), OR (b) align the LLM audit judge prompt to not penalize decorative/seal image markers in hierarchical docs where text extraction is complete. Option (b) is simpler and arguably more correct since the 12 markers are likely decorative seals/logos in a 502-node/110k-char document with zero content loss.

root_causes.root_cause: _inject_arabic_structural_headings (RFC-027 D4, converters.py:85-115) has two bugs causing Arabic structural markers to not be promoted to ATX headings: (1) prev_blank guard requires a blank line before each marker but OCR output from scanned Arabic PDFs flows continuously without blank-line separators, so only the first article gets promoted; (2) len(t)<=60 char limit is too tight for Arabic legal headings that include article titles (common lines are 66-76+ chars). Both bugs compound to produce flat/depth-0/depth-1 trees for Arabic legal docs despite clean text extraction.
root_causes.code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/converters.py::_inject_arabic_structural_headings -> md_to_tree (flat tree) -> validate_tree (depth<2) -> flat success path (cat_b_promoted)
root_causes.suggested_fix: (1) Remove or relax the prev_blank guard: instead of requiring the prior line to be blank, check whether the line STARTS with an Arabic structural marker regardless of prior context (the len<=60/80 guard already filters mid-paragraph references). (2) Raise the char limit from 60 to at least 100 to accommodate Arabic article headings with titles. Both changes are in _inject_arabic_structural_headings, ~5-10 lines changed.

The Haftpflicht-Besondere-Bedingungen doc uses Roman-numeral sub-levels (I through XXVII) as its 27-clause sub-structure, which the ordinal splitter cannot detect, leaving the tree at depth-2 when it should be depth-3+.

root_causes.root_cause: GHV-TKV-Tarif.pdf has 3 rate tables (horse/dog/cat) collapsed into unsegmented leaf blobs with leaf_concentration=0.39. Table rows are inherently not heading-like markers, so neither md_to_tree (which only splits on ATX headings) nor split_oversized_leaf_nodes (which only splits on ordinal/paragraph markers) can segment them. This is an architectural gap: there is no table-row-as-structural-marker detection. RFC-027 D5 proposed raising the small_doc_promoted threshold but that only changes the verdict, not the structure.
root_causes.code_path: md_to_tree (no headings in table content) -> split_oversized_leaf_nodes (no ordinal markers in table rows)
root_causes.suggested_fix: Add table-aware splitting to split_oversized_leaf_nodes: detect markdown pipe-table boundaries (lines matching |...|...|) and split oversized leaves at table-boundary transitions. Alternatively, in the converter, inject synthetic heading markers between distinct tables (e.g. when a blank line separates two table blocks). ~40-60 lines.

root_causes.root_cause: RFC-027 D7 dynamic timeout scaling was implemented as dead code: chunked_docling_timeout_s() exists in converters.py but is never imported or called by worker.py. The worker always uses fixed CHILD_TIMEOUT=1770s (29.5min). world-stats-pocketbook-2023.pdf (292 pages, 6.4MB) requires 24-49 min for Docling conversion at 5-10s/page on CPU. With 2 chunks of ~150 pages each, total processing can exceed the fixed 1770s timeout, causing the worker to SIGTERM/SIGKILL the child subprocess before any artifacts are persisted.
root_causes.code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/worker.py::_run_converter_subprocess -> asyncio.timeout(CHILD_TIMEOUT) [line 245]; src/pageindex_mcp/converters.py::chunked_docling_timeout_s [line 2182, dead code]
root_causes.suggested_fix: Wire chunked_docling_timeout_s into _run_converter_subprocess: (1) accept an optional timeout_override parameter in _run_converter_subprocess, (2) in converters_cli, after chunked conversion, emit chunk_count in the stdout JSON, (3) OR pre-compute the expected timeout in the worker before spawning the child by reading the page count from the staged file. Simplest approach: have converters_cli emit the dynamic timeout as part of a pre-flight page-count check, or increase CHILD_TIMEOUT to accommodate the chunked path (e.g. 3600s) and let JOB_TIMEOUT follow.

root_causes.root_cause: _is_garbled_blob checks PUA (U+E000-U+F8FF) at 3% threshold but has NO check for Arabic Presentation Forms (U+FB50-FDFF, U+FE70-FEFF). These are positional glyph variants that indicate font-encoded garble, but they are valid Unicode points outside PUA range. _infer_script (line 962) counts them as Arabic (lines 971-976), reinforcing the false-negative. Documents with 93%+ presentation forms pass all garble checks and store PASS verdict.
root_causes.code_path: helpers.py::_is_garbled_blob (line 879-881 PUA check) -> _infer_script (line 971-976 counts FB50-FEFF as Arabic) -> _tree_is_garbled -> validate_tree -> classify_verdict stores PASS
root_causes.suggested_fix: Add a presentation-forms ratio check in _is_garbled_blob, after the PUA check. Count chars in U+FB50-FDFF and U+FE70-FEFF ranges; if ratio exceeds threshold (e.g., 0.50 of total Arabic chars), return True. This catches documents where text extraction emitted positional glyph forms instead of logical Arabic Unicode.

root_causes.root_cause: _tree_is_rtl_reversed (RFC-027 D3) compares _arabic_readability_score for forward vs get_display() reversed text, but _arabic_readability_score only checks 14 _AR_COMMON_WORDS and _AR_DEFINITE_RE matches. For specialized vocabulary (governance, data policy) where sampled lines contain no common words and word-level reversal preserves definite-article pattern, both orig_total and disp_total are 0 or equal, so disp_total > orig_total is False and reversal goes undetected. validate_tree returns (True, '') and stored verdict is PASS with empty reason.
root_causes.code_path: helpers.py::_tree_is_rtl_reversed (line 1047-1089) -> _arabic_readability_score (converters.py line 1341-1348) -> _AR_COMMON_WORDS (14 words) -> validate_tree (line 1129) returns True -> classify_verdict stores PASS
root_causes.suggested_fix: Expand _arabic_readability_score with additional signals: (1) add governance/legal domain words to _AR_COMMON_WORDS (حوكمة, بيانات, سياسة, إدارة, تنظيم, قرار, etc.); (2) add a character-level reversal check -- reversed Arabic characters produce morphologically invalid sequences (final-form chars at word start, initial-form at word end) that can be detected without vocabulary dependence; (3) consider bigram frequency analysis as a vocabulary-independent readability signal.

root_causes.root_cause: Arabic PDFs with custom font encoding (PUA glyphs in U+E000-F8FF) or scanned-only content defeat both text-layer extraction and OCR fallback. root_causes.code_path: client.py line 721-741 (D3a probe) -> PRE_GARBLE_FORCE_OCR_ENABLED=false -> Fix-3 retry (line 984) -> converters.py tesseract_ocr_pdf_pages -> near-zero/junk output
root_causes.suggested_fix: Two-pronged: (1) For PUA-encoded PDFs (القرار التنظيمي): when OCR escalation also fails (output < LOW_CONTENT_OCR_CHAR_FLOOR after retry), attempt rasterize-then-OCR as a final fallback -- bypass the corrupt text layer entirely by rendering pages as images and OCR-ing the raster. Both require per-doc investigation to validate feasibility.

For specialized vocabulary (governance, data policy) where sampled lines contain no common words and word-level reversal preserves definite-article pattern, both orig_total and disp_total are 0 or equal, so disp_total > orig_total is False and reversal goes undetected. validate_tree returns (True, '') and stored verdict is PASS with empty reason.

root_causes.suggested_fix: Expand _arabic_readability_score with additional signals: (1) add governance/legal domain words to _AR_COMMON_WORDS (حوكمة, بيانات, سياسة, إدارة, تنظيم, قرار, etc.); (2) add a character-level reversal check -- reversed Arabic characters produce morphologically invalid sequences (final-form chars at word start, initial-form at word end) that can be detected without vocabulary dependence; (3) consider bigram frequency analysis as a vocabulary-independent readability signal.

(2) For scanned PDFs producing only numeric junk (وارد 597): add post-OCR Arabic content validation -- if OCR output has 0 Arabic chars on a document with Arabic filename, flag as extraction failure rather than storing junk.
